Definition: % of Windows systems with all required patches applied within SLA windows at any given point in time.
Level 1 - Ad Hoc: No formal patching. Compliance unknown. Patches applied only after incidents.
Level 2 - Developing: Patching occurs inconsistently. Manually tracked. <70% compliance. Significant gaps.
Level 3 - Defined: Documented patch schedule. Tooling used (WSUS/SCCM/Intune). 70-89% compliance.
Level 4 - Managed: Automated deployment with exception management. 90-95% compliance. SLA breaches escalated.
Level 5 - Optimized: Zero-touch automated patching. >95% compliance. Integrated with vulnerability management. Real-time dashboards.

Definition: Average elapsed time from patch release by Microsoft to successful deployment across the estate, measured by severity tier.
Level 1 - Ad Hoc: No SLA defined. Patches applied weeks or months after release, if ever.
Level 2 - Developing: Informal SLA rarely met. Critical patches take >30 days. No severity tiering.
Level 3 - Defined: SLA defined by severity (Critical 14 days, High 30 days). Tracked but not always met.
Level 4 - Managed: SLA consistently met: Critical 7 days, High 14 days, Medium 30 days. Exceptions tracked.
Level 5 - Optimized: Critical patches deployed within 72 hours. Automated pipeline with pre-tested packages. Real-time SLA reporting.

Definition: % of patch attempts that fail and require manual intervention or re-execution before compliance is achieved.
Level 1 - Ad Hoc: Failures not tracked. Patching done manually with no visibility into success or failure.
Level 2 - Developing: Some failures logged but no root cause analysis. Failure rate >15%. Remediation is reactive.
Level 3 - Defined: Failures tracked in patching tool. Rate between 5-15%. Basic retry logic exists.
Level 4 - Managed: Failure rate <5%. Root cause analysis performed. Automated retry and remediation workflows.
Level 5 - Optimized: Failure rate <1%. Pre-deployment staging tests. Self-healing remediation scripts. Continuous improvement of package quality.

Definition: % of CIS Windows Benchmark controls passing across the managed estate, assessed via automated scanning tools such as Nessus, Qualys, or Microsoft Secure Score.
Level 1 - Ad Hoc: No awareness or application of CIS benchmarks. No hardening baseline defined.
Level 2 - Developing: Ad hoc hardening applied. No formal benchmark adopted. Score below 50%.
Level 3 - Defined: CIS benchmark adopted. Automated scanning in place. Score between 50-75%.
Level 4 - Managed: Score between 75-90%. Exceptions documented with risk acceptance. Remediation tracked.
Level 5 - Optimized: Score above 90% consistently. Benchmark enforced in golden image. Continuous compliance drift detection.

Definition: % of Windows endpoints with an active, up-to-date endpoint protection or EDR solution deployed and reporting telemetry.
Level 1 - Ad Hoc: No centralised endpoint protection. Antivirus deployed ad hoc or not at all.
Level 2 - Developing: Antivirus deployed on most systems but not centrally managed. Gaps exist. No EDR.
Level 3 - Defined: Centralised AV/EPP deployed on more than 90% of estate. Managed console with reporting.
Level 4 - Managed: EDR deployed across more than 95% of estate. Alerts integrated with SIEM. Automated response.
Level 5 - Optimized: 100% EDR coverage. AI-driven threat detection. Automated containment. Zero blind spots.

Definition: % of Windows endpoints with full-disk encryption enforced via BitLocker, with recovery keys escrowed centrally.
Level 1 - Ad Hoc: No encryption enforced. No policy in place.
Level 2 - Developing: BitLocker enabled on some devices. No central key escrow. Inconsistent enforcement.
Level 3 - Defined: BitLocker enforced via GPO on more than 80% of endpoints. Keys stored in AD or Intune.
Level 4 - Managed: 100% encryption on all portable devices. Keys centrally managed. Compliance reporting automated.
Level 5 - Optimized: 100% coverage including desktops. Pre-boot authentication enforced. Key rotation automated. Audit-ready.

Definition: % of Windows systems using Microsoft Local Administrator Password Solution (LAPS) to manage and rotate unique local admin passwords per device.
Level 1 - Ad Hoc: Shared or static local admin passwords in use across the estate.
Level 2 - Developing: LAPS deployed on some systems. Large portions still using shared passwords.
Level 3 - Defined: LAPS deployed on more than 70% of estate. Policy defined. Some manual password management remains.
Level 4 - Managed: LAPS deployed on more than 95% of estate. Automated rotation. Integrated with PAM solution.
Level 5 - Optimized: 100% LAPS coverage. Integrated with enterprise PAM. Automated audit and anomaly detection.

Definition: % of Active Directory accounts inactive for more than 90 days that have not been reviewed, disabled, or removed.
Level 1 - Ad Hoc: No account lifecycle process. Stale accounts accumulate indefinitely. No review performed.
Level 2 - Developing: Periodic manual reviews occur. More than 15% of accounts are stale. No automation.
Level 3 - Defined: Quarterly reviews scheduled. Stale accounts below 10%. Semi-automated discovery in place.
Level 4 - Managed: Automated stale account detection. Below 5% stale. Monthly review cycle with auto-disable.
Level 5 - Optimized: Below 1% stale accounts. Automated lifecycle management. Joiners, movers, leavers fully automated.

Definition: % of user accounts for which multi-factor authentication is enforced for all access to Windows systems and management planes.
Level 1 - Ad Hoc: No MFA enforced. Password-only authentication across all systems.
Level 2 - Developing: MFA available but optional. Adopted by less than 50% of users. Privileged accounts unprotected.
Level 3 - Defined: MFA enforced for all privileged accounts and remote access. Regular users partially covered.
Level 4 - Managed: MFA enforced for more than 95% of all accounts. Conditional Access policies in place.
Level 5 - Optimized: 100% MFA with phishing-resistant methods such as FIDO2 or Windows Hello. Zero exceptions.

Definition: % of Active Directory Group Policy Objects applied as intended, with no configuration drift between defined policy and actual system state.
Level 1 - Ad Hoc: GPOs exist but are not managed or audited. Significant drift and conflicts present.
Level 2 - Developing: GPOs defined but poorly documented. Drift not detected. Manual audits rarely performed.
Level 3 - Defined: GPO structure documented. Quarterly compliance checks. Drift detected via tooling.
Level 4 - Managed: GPO compliance above 90%. Automated drift detection with alerting. Changes tracked in change management.
Level 5 - Optimized: GPO compliance above 98%. All changes via approved pipeline. Drift auto-remediated. Full audit trail.

Definition: % of scheduled uptime during which Windows systems are available and fully operational, excluding planned maintenance windows.
Level 1 - Ad Hoc: No uptime tracking. Availability unknown. Outages managed entirely reactively.
Level 2 - Developing: Basic uptime monitoring via ping. Availability approximately 95%. No SLA defined.
Level 3 - Defined: Agent-based monitoring deployed. Availability tracked against SLA. Targeting 99%.
Level 4 - Managed: 99.5% availability achieved. Automated alerting and escalation. Capacity planning in place.
Level 5 - Optimized: 99.9% or higher availability. Predictive failure detection. Automated failover. Zero unplanned outages per quarter.

Definition: % of Windows systems whose security, application, and system event logs are centrally collected, parsed, and alerted on in real time.
Level 1 - Ad Hoc: No centralised log collection. Logs reviewed only after incidents occur.
Level 2 - Developing: Logs collected from some systems to a central store. No real-time alerting.
Level 3 - Defined: More than 80% of systems sending logs to SIEM. Basic alert rules defined. Reviewed regularly.
Level 4 - Managed: More than 95% log coverage. Correlated alerts. Automated triage for common events.
Level 5 - Optimized: 100% coverage. AI-driven anomaly detection. Automated response playbooks. SOC-integrated.

Definition: % of Windows systems running OS versions that have reached End-of-Life and no longer receive security updates from Microsoft.
Level 1 - Ad Hoc: No lifecycle tracking. Significant EOL OS in production such as Windows Server 2008 or Windows 7.
Level 2 - Developing: EOL systems identified but no formal remediation plan. More than 20% of estate on EOL OS.
Level 3 - Defined: EOL inventory maintained. Remediation plan in place. Between 5-20% of estate on EOL OS.
Level 4 - Managed: Below 5% EOL OS. Upgrade projects tracked. ESU licensing managed where unavoidable.
Level 5 - Optimized: Zero EOL OS in production. Lifecycle roadmap proactively managed. OS upgrades automated.

Definition: Age and patch state of the base OS image used for provisioning new Windows systems, measured by time since last update.
Level 1 - Ad Hoc: No golden image. Systems built manually each time. No standardisation.
Level 2 - Developing: Golden image exists but updated infrequently, more than 6 months old. Manual build process.
Level 3 - Defined: Golden image updated quarterly. Includes current patches. Stored in image library.
Level 4 - Managed: Golden image updated monthly. Automated build pipeline. Validation tests run before release.
Level 5 - Optimized: Golden image updated with every patch cycle. Fully automated build, test, and release pipeline. Zero manual steps.

Definition: % of new Windows system builds delivered via automated provisioning tools such as MDT, SCCM, Intune Autopilot, or Ansible, versus manual installation.
Level 1 - Ad Hoc: All systems built manually. No automation. Build time exceeds 4 hours per system.
Level 2 - Developing: Automation tools available but used inconsistently. Less than 50% of builds automated.
Level 3 - Defined: Between 50-80% of builds automated. Standard process defined. Build time under 2 hours.
Level 4 - Managed: More than 90% automated provisioning. Build time under 45 minutes. Self-service for standard builds.
Level 5 - Optimized: 100% automated provisioning. Zero-touch deployment. Build time under 15 minutes. Full auditability.

Definition: % of scheduled backup jobs for Windows systems that complete successfully without error within the defined backup window.
Level 1 - Ad Hoc: No formalised backups. Data loss risk is high. Backups done ad hoc if at all.
Level 2 - Developing: Backups configured but not monitored. Success rate below 85%. Recovery never tested.
Level 3 - Defined: Backups monitored. Success rate between 85-95%. Recovery tested annually.
Level 4 - Managed: Success rate above 98%. Failures trigger automated alerts and retries. Recovery tested quarterly.
Level 5 - Optimized: Above 99.5% success rate. Automated recovery testing. RTOs and RPOs validated continuously. Immutable backups.

Definition: The ability to detect when a Windows system's actual configuration deviates from its approved baseline, and the speed of remediation.
Level 1 - Ad Hoc: No baseline defined. Configuration drift is unknown and undetected.
Level 2 - Developing: Baseline documented but drift not actively monitored. Manual periodic audits only.
Level 3 - Defined: Drift detection tooling deployed on more than 70% of estate. Alerts generated on deviation.
Level 4 - Managed: Drift detected and alerted within 1 hour on more than 90% of estate. Auto-remediation for common deviations.
Level 5 - Optimized: Real-time drift detection across 100% of estate. Auto-remediation within minutes. Full audit trail.
